script.stored_text_completeness: All 17630 canonical characters read sequentially in full in 1 bounded ranges; auto-generated untimed text; stored ending is complete ("go do literally anything else."); ASR name drift (Priya rendered "Preus" and "Bree"; "1,000 $300"); includes a self-promotional "school community" call and a not-financial-advice disclaimer; 3,206 words over 1,150 seconds (~167 wpm) is consistent with a full read; audio, timed delivery and editing unverified.
script.opening_words: The best investor in your entire office is the woman who forgot her account existed. Not Danny two desks over refreshing a trading app through a cracked phone screen at every red light. Danny has made about 200 trades this year. Priya in accounting has made exactly one back in 2019. And then she lost the password and never logged in again. Guess which one is winning. My name is Nick and I've spent an embarrassing amount of my life
script.ending_words: from me today, let it be this. The market pays you to sit still. So, the next time your brain begs you to do something clever with your money, remember that clever is expensive, boring is free. And the laziest person in the room is usually the one on her way to a million dollars. Set it up once, forget the password on purpose, and go do literally anything else.
script.analysis: Full 17630 canonical characters read. A passive-investing essay framed by Danny (active trader) vs Priya (forgot her account): SPIVA underperformance and persistence, Magellan investor-return anecdote, Dalbar behavior gap, missing best days, employer match, target-date funds, lump sum vs DCA, compounding ($500/month), Bogle fee math, account limits, Fidelity 401(k) millionaires, an honest caveat on surplus income and lower forecasts, sequence risk, simple-vs-easy discipline, a community plug and disclaimer. Verified: SPIVA 2024 summary (no category majority outperforming over 15 years), 2026 limits; Bogle, Dalbar, JPM best-days and fee arithmetic reproduce. Unverified/overstated: exact ~90% and "zero" persistence; Magellan investors "lost money"; $987K implies ~9.4%; waiting 10 years costs ~two-thirds, not half; thumbnail $50->$2M unsupported. The stored ending is complete.
beat_map: Cold open: forgotten account beats active trader.
Defining lazy: decide once, automate, do not touch.
Magellan investors and the soap analogy.
Missing the best days; time in the market.
Target-date/total-market fund; lump sum vs DCA.
Fees: Bogle tyranny of compounding costs.
Honest caveats: surplus income, lower forecasts, sequence risk.
Simple vs easy; community plug; disclaimer and close.
